Developed by Elder Games and published by Merge Games & Headup Games, Meridian: Squad 22 is the sequel to one of my favorite real time strategy games made by an indie dev team. And I take some liberties on the term “dev team” since this title, much like the first one in this series, was also the hard work of a single very talented man: Ede Tarsoly. To create an RTS such as Meridian: New World took some effort. But to go further than that and launch another game just two years apart which irons out almost all the previous one’s flaws, is a feat truly worthy of admiration.

Meridian: Squad 22 is once again, a strategy game driven by a storyline. The novelty to this sequel however, is that a certain number of choices you undertake during some missions, will affect the following ones and subsequently the rest of the campaign. This provides us with a well deserved replay value even if the game itself is anything but short. I was most pleased to see that the pathfinding and general confusion of the AI on the map, are issues long gone. The skirmish mode takes place on randomly-generated maps so you always have an extra challenge, apart from the enemies which will be more aggressive this time around. In Squad 22 we now have the full spectrum of warfare, with the inclusion of both aerial and naval units compared to the the previous title’s predominantly land-based troops.
The game is richly detailed, from both the texture quality of the units & terrain and even the research tree, which really encourages you to explore and find research canisters (a shout-out to Starcraft 2’s brilliant tech advancement choices). You can’t really complain that this wouldn’t be a strategy title worthy of 2016’s relatively high standards.

The sound score has been composed by Hexany Audio and it truly gives this game, a soundtrack to match its looks and Sci-Fi atmosphere. And as expected, the voice acting is on par with the rest of the game sounds. An obvious step forward in regards to the less than enthusiastic voice work from New World.

+ Beautiful graphics and soundtrack
+ Steam Trading Cards & Achievements

- Still no multiplayer modes
Squad 22 is a clear example that you don’t need immense budgets, to create a fully functioning and aesthetically pleasing strategy title any longer. What a small team of highly talented people have proved, is how far we’re come in terms of game design over the last few years. As polished as this game is right now, the Early Access label should not deter anyone from purchasing it. Steam Achievements and Trading Cards are just the icing on the cake at this point.
The only thing that sucks about this game is the voice acting. Otherwise it's fantastic. Very retro, very fun, and the soundtrack is spectacular.

It's very rare to play an RPG that does not feature a globe trotting, world saving, massive journey taking main character--And it's even rarer to do that
. Yet here we are with CDPR's incredibly crafted sequel to the legendary Witcher 1, and they have absolutely captured lightning in a bottle once again. Following the events of the previous installment's ending, players find themselves assuming the role of Geralt of Rivia once more as he's tasked with ensuring King Faltest's safety during a major battle to regain heirs to the throne. When an assassin catches the witcher off guard and commits regicide, Geralt sets off on a quest with Dandelion, Triss, Zoltan, and newcomer Roche to capture the kingslayer and the witcher's name. Throughout the three chapters within the Witcher 2, players will encounter sorceresses who are not what they seem, great beasts intent on killing everything in their path, kings who see the witcher as a pawn to do their bidding, and a troll that gets drunk and ignores his bridge duties, among other things.
While the Witcher 1's combat was generally regarded as clunky but servicable, the Witcher 2's combat greatly innovates the concept and improves in nearly every single way. The gameplay could possibly be regarded as a hack and slash, but you absolutely won't get away with simply diving into battle and swinging with wild abandon, lest you want to load your save fifty times in a row--players must tactically dodge, roll, and parry with every strike and use all available resources in order to survive. This simply isn't like previous game in which the player can skirt by without ever coating their blade in oil or drinking only Swallows--the Witcher 2 will kick your♥♥♥♥♥with its difficulty.
Storywise, the Witcher 2 is stronger than ever. The mature themes and writing the Witcher series is known for continue to pervade throughout this sequel, with gritty realism and bleakness factoring into the story's plots and subplots. Choices have to be made, and these choices are never good versus evil, but rather the lesser of two evils or a mixture of gray scaled justice and consequence. Choices you made in the Witcher 1 will come back to bite you or remind you of just who you are, and choices you make here will reveal after effects--some soon, some later. Everything matters.
As for a few short remarks, the music is almost as excellent as the first series' entry, though perhaps not as memorable. The voice acting is leagues ahead of the Witcher 1 as well as the characters' models themselves. Indeed, the graphics and art style of the Witcher 2 look
beautiful, and I can only imagine what the Witcher 3 will look like.
Overall, just like its predecessor, the Witcher 2 is an excellent CRPG with a few minor flaws, but otherwise is near perfection in gameplay, story telling, and building a breathing, believable world where the stakes are high and the choices have impact. If you are questioning whether or not you should start your Witcher journey, I wholeheartedly recommend you begin with the Witcher 1 and then make your way here. For those who have finished the Witcher 1 and are wondering if its sequel is just as good, I will tell you this: it is better, and it is incredible.

It shares a similar vein to Miami Hotline but is different by valuing stealth over speed. It also has partially procedurally generated levels in that the items used for killing can vary each time you restart a level.
So far, all I've sung were praises. However, this game is far from perfect and the developer should fix these things right away.
1. I can clearly see that the variable weapons/traps in earlier levels are well thought out and polished. However, as the levels go on, the levels become clearly more linear in that the items are the same in each restart. This is not necessarily a problem for all players but as Party Hard favors stealth (biding your time) over a quick massacre, a lack of variables equates to less playability for some. (Especially since there are only 4 characters)
2. A slightly bigger problem, but not necessarily game breaking. In appropriate animations at certain points. People sleeping standing up after dropping them from carrying them. Carrying people without using any hands at all. People floating across the map without initiating the walking animation. All aesthetic stuff since I still had a good time up to this point.
3. Here's the game breaking bug: upon finishing the game and starting as the newly unlocked character, I was unable to bury bodies or interact with traps. Which is vital to completing the game. And since I never (SPOILER) used the 3rd character in the first playthrough, I was wanting to unlock him by completing the second playthrough. Unfortunately, being unable to do anything else other than stab and run, will make that impossible. Trust me, I could not have gone through all the levels on the first playthrough by relying only on my knife and my terrible cardio. (The character in game runs as well as a morbidly obese being).
That being said, I do recommend the game because I felt that it was worth $9.92. But for those looking for a game with good replayability, I suggest watching a few gameplay videos and read a few more reviews before making a final decision because I personally do not think the game is worth any more than $9.92.

+
Can you believe it?
+ Visually the game looks absolutely stunning for an RTS. Tons of detail. The grass, and trees sway in the wind. Bright vivid neon styled colors for many of the projectiles and units that all add to this futuristic Sci-Fi appeal. Great explosions and particle effects.
+ The gameplay is a load of fun especially if you enjoy other RTS games. I'd consider it a mix between Starcraft 2 and Command and Conquer. I had no problem hopping straight into this game, everything felt natural.
+ A research / tech tree that follows you throughout the game. This encourages you to explore the maps to discover research cannisters which will allow you to unlock new units, upgrades, turrets, production perks, and so fourth.
+ Ground, Air, and Navel Units.  They all seem well balanced, and it honestly looks fantastic to have a large group go to battle with another large group.
+ A pretty decent story. You are about 1000 years into the future, and Earth is overpoulated. A colony ship was sent out to find a new planet to inhabit Meridian. Their communications were cut off. Earth sends Squad 22 to go investigate.
+ Epic soundtrack
+ Conquest Mode, which is basically skirmish battles against AI at differing difficulty levels 1v1 while taking over plots to take over the world.
- In campaign, if one of your "main characters" dies you lose the mission and have to restart. This is incredibly annoying as they tend to look similar to regular infantry with slightly more health. The enemy AI tends to focus fire on one unit at the time, so if they focus on one of your heroes you may suddenly lose the mission. :(
- The UI is a bit too small, especially when trying to read dialogue. I think it should be enlarged or perhaps add an option to.
- Campaign is unfinished, but that is to be expected.
~ Single-Player Only. Some people may be turned off by this as RTS games are known for their multiplayer. Personally I think focusing on the story and missions is a great thing  as many RTS games of late have had pretty boring campaigns. The missions in Meridian: Squad 22 feel meaningful and challenging.

MechaNika is a very funny and charming game about a young girl with aspirations of world domination.
From beginning to end, it delivers satisfying puzzles, on-point humor, cute graphics, and surprisingly dark themes. Do not make the mistake of thinking that this is a game for children -- I promise that it's really not. It often deals with very creepy and adult issues like cults, murder, pickled punks, and very, uh, interesting relationships between humans and animals. If any of this offends you then you're looking at the wrong game.
But if you're thinking "Sign me up!" then you've come to the right place. MechaNika is a real gem of a point and click adventure game. It will keep you laughing the whole time with its witty humor and observations about humanity. The whole game is laid out in such a way that nothing feels too difficult or repetitive. As a result, it's a slightly short game, but that's not really a bad thing because there's no filler to get bogged down in. You're also given a bit of leeway in how you can solve some of the puzzles which is a nice touch.
Definitely recommended. The devs put a lot of love into this game, and it's absolutely worth playing.

Don't Starve Together is a deceptively hard survival game, I say deceptively hard because the learning curve leans more towards the ability to memorize mob patterns and preparing for the various dangers the game will throw your way. I HIGHLY recommend experiencing the game for yourself before looking up any guides from seasoned Don't Starve players; there are more efficient ways to play, but the game allows you to play however you want via World Settings and the amazing mods offered on Steam's Workshop. It is all a matter of preference and you shouldn't feel discouraged if your playstyle is "frowned upon" by the more experienced.
Still, there is some general etiquette to playing on servers with others. Some players new or old may not mind, but these general guidelines should improve your skills as a team player if you do choose to join servers:
-Be considerate, do not pick every resource close to where you spawn. Think of other players who will join that will need the resources.
-Do not ask where the base is! Instead you can forage for the first few days and ask your fellow players what resources are needed. You can easily find the base on your own, some servers even build their base right on the spawn.
-Don't sit in base. Period. Unless you are preparing for a fight, cooking, or organizing food and items, please do not just sit there doing nothing. Do not waste valuable time and hunger.
-NEVER pick flowers! They spawn Butterflies which can be easily killed for Butterfly Wings (a free food source for every season except Winter) and Butter (rare drop and long spoilage ingredient for various Crock Pot Recipes). I know this seems insignificant, but why throw away free food like that?
-Accept any criticisms thrown your way and let it be a learning experience, as even if you do something wrong, think of it as another way to learn the game's mechanics.
The fun parts of the game can come from the learning experience of playing, but once you've learned more than just the basics, there is a whole slew of content waiting...IF you can handle the challenge. You can eventually go to the caves, which are a whole new world teeming with dangerous mobs but valuable resources! In the caves also lies the Ruins, which have some of the best gear and resources in the game. In addition to the Seasonal Giants, there are also mightier bosses with immense health and damage designed for multiple players to tackle. If that's not enough for you, there are many events that occur during the seasons, moon phases, and Klei's Holiday events which mean there is a lot to do in each unique world! You can fight every boss, amass the best loot, have a huge surplus of food and supplies, all while expanding/decorating your base if you so choose! The game will let you play however you want to play, but be prepared to overcome the challenges that come with such a luxury.
Should you buy this game? Absolutely. Is it the perfect game at its core? That's up for you to decide; personally there are various issues I have with the game and to an extent its community, but you could pass them off as nitpicks to an otherwise amazing experience.
<PROS>
-Plentiful content, there is much to do in each individual world and players to lend a helping hand.
-High learning curve, usually a bad thing for new players but it's all part of the amazing experience.
-Mod support, optional but can improve your experience if you choose to install any. Mods range from various quality of life additions, visual changes, gameplay changes, fixes, playable custom characters, and more.
-Skins and cosmetics, given four times weekly if you play enough. Resets on Thursday. The game practically gives you gifts no matter how you play.
-Freedom of playstyle, the game can be a combination of Sandbox, Roguelike, pure Survival, PvP, or Management Game if you choose to play it so.
-A sense of accomplishment for mastering the game's mechanics, helping out players, and building your world how you want it.
<CONS>
-You will meet unsavory players on servers throughout your playtime, as with a lot of other games.
-Tedious tasks, such as gathering certain resources, crafting certain items, and fighting certain mobs. The game has unconventional means of doing tasks en masse such as cooking a stack of foods on the fire pit or feeding meats to a bird to produce eggs.
-Early on the Seasons can prove to be quite overwhelming and restrictive, but learning to prepare for them means you can always overcome and even take advantage of the obstacles that come Seasonally. One tip I can give you is that the items you craft from the Seasonal Giants will usually help you in other seasons; the Eyebrella you can craft from a Deerclops Eyeball provides 100% protection against the rain and thunder in Spring, while in the Summer it keeps you cool for a long period of time.
-Flaws in the game mechanics, the devs have tinkered with the game's items for better or worse. One example I'm going to throw from out of the blue is Marble, used to craft various items but also the Marble Suit. The Marble Suit encourages tanking enemies which can be a bad habit for new players to learn, but other than that it's useful for servers where you can't kite enemies. The biggest problem with Marble, and many of the game's other resources, is that they require much grinding to gather and maintain. Of course, these materials are OPTIONAL to how you play. Going back to tedious tasks, the game can be a management sim if you let it. Kudos if you enjoy the good old grind.
<The Community>
There are wonderful members of the community like any other game. You'll find all types of players on Twitch, Youtube, and the Klei Forums where they post and discuss. In such communities, you will also meet unsavory folk who share contraversial opinions and can be aggressive towards all types of players. Of course, they are only opinions and you should know not to blindly follow anything these members may deem "correct". One very contraversial member of the Don't Starve Community is Edgy Rick, and he is named that for a reason. On one hand I enjoy his playstyle, being highly efficient and catered to experienced players; Edgy Rick teaches to avoid the noob traps of this game, but enforces this playstyle and deems every other playstyle inferior. Of course for the sake of being Edgy he does this, but it's highly discouraging and DEGRADING to new players who stumble upon his content.
<The Bottom Line>
Overall, this game is amazing for its depth and charm. Don't Starve Together is hands down one of the best games I've played, surpassing its category of "Survival" games and offering much more to the table than just crafting and exploring. Let me just remind you, for the billionth time in this review, to play the game how you see fit.
I give this game a genuine 10/10, and for new players I give a pat on the back and a warm welcome to the world of Don't Starve Together.

Medieval II Total War is a RTS (real time sratergy) of sorts that lets you play as one of the medieval super powers of that age, each with their own strengths and weaknesses.
For example France has the best knights in the game but suffers when it comes to infantry whether they be archers or spear men. But England has worse knights but better foot soldiers.
When starting the game the player has a number of options (besides the options menu and quiting the game of course). I have not covered  multiplayer in this review as I have no idea if any of the public servers work as I have never tried any of them,  but the single player,  oh boy i can tell you,  that it is good.
First off the game gives you a custom battle mode. So, if you ever wondered what it would be like to have an army of nothing but peasants charge a fully equipped renaissance castle filled to the brim with archers with flaming arows, now you can find out!
Then there's the campaign which might be confusing to some, but I suggest either looking up some hints and tips on the forums or replaying the tutorial. The campaign also has diplomacy, and very good diplomacy at that. And the best part is, the A.I does make deals with you that are in your favour, such as giving you gold or line of sight to where they live if you ally with them. As well as that there are spies for taking a peek at what your foes are doing and how big a force they have, as well as assasins for when you just need to go all stabby, stabby on that certain duke or king.
Even though the graphics are not up to date whith what todays graphics are, they still look good even if you zoom right in on people's faces.
That, and the way a castle looks when you bring its walls down with everyone on top falling through the new hole you just made, is awsome.
The game also involves a lot of strategy. I can tell. And even if you sort of suck at it, like I do, you can still have a lot of fun witth this game. Basic tactics (allthough not as good) can still win you the game, at least against the medium A.I. as charging your entire hourse-back army down a hill to smash into your foe's unprotected rear is a tactic.
Also, this game handles flaming projectiles really well, as hitting your enemy's peasants feels really satisfying, as well as making you really glad that you are not one of  those poor fools. This goes for catapults and trebuchets as well, exept bigger and much more deadly ones. You can also make enemy siege weapons burn down, which makes you feel like such a troll to the stupid A.I.  As you say "nope!" as your archers burn down an entire siege tower and the men who were just using it are forced to use ladders, only to be poked to death by your spear-men, now waiting at the top for them.
So, all in all, I give it a 9/10 as there are some things that bug me a little, such as 1 guy with a leather shield blocking 10 arrows at once or a knight in full plate-mail bursting into flames at the first fire arrow.

At first glance, this game may seem simple; however, it's anything but.
You start off with simple levels and enemies, collecting items that will help (or sometimes harm) you, getting you ready to fight progressively tougher enemies. Each time you go to the next level, you are met with different enemies, and all new opportunities to get items. And just when you think you've beat the game...you haven't. I'll let you figure out what that means.
The items, enemies, rooms, and level layouts are completely random, so you will likely never have the same exact experience in this game twice. Unlocking new characters adds to the experience, as each one has its own benefits and setbacks, making the game easier in some ways and harder in others. Because of the overwhelming amount of items and enemies, I'd always recommend playing with the wiki for the game open, just so that you never make a bad decision when it comes to picking up items. Still, some things in this game come with a learning curve and you'll just have to find out what items you like to use and which ones will make you rage.
It'll be frustrating at first, but once you unlock more items and beat your own personal records, you'll be addicted. Buying the Wrath of the Lamb DLC makes the game even tougher (so I suggest buying it after you have a good feel for the base game), but adds loads of new content, including enemies, items, levels, and more.
Honestly, I'd recommend this game to anyone I knew, even with all of the dark humor and blasphemous jokes. When you look past all of that, it's a great game with excellent replay value.

Otherwise you best steer clear for fear of tripping and falling down a rabbit hole from whence your real life will never return.  Im only slightly joking.
There are two games I have ever played that I truly love on one hand and truly regret on the other.  The first is Dark Souls, which drained away my entire year of 2011. The second, is this game and its predecessor, Terran Conflict.  I have played X3 for probably 1000 hours and it was a major contributing factor to my college GPA dropping seriously about 3 full tenths of a point and leading to a few failed classes that I had to stay an extra semester to retake.  There were other factors too dont get me wrong, but seriously if you don't have a healthy lifestyle to fall back on and you are a sucker for space sim type games this game might hook you and never let go until one day you stumble out of your apartment, blinded by the sun, realizing you havent shaved in 8 months and have lost 30 pounds and arent sure what year it is or what happened to your life or any of the people you used to know.  It is simultaneously the best and most dangerous thing you can buy for twenty dollars.  Whats sadder still is my hard drive failed and so I literally have nothing to show for at least 800 hours of my life.  Holy Sh!t.
I tell you all this because theres no way to sum up what you can actually do in the game in any reasonable amount of words, but heres a few useful bits I have divided rather arbitrarily into 3 good points and 3 not as good points.
Good stuff:
1: Think of EVE Online, except its a single-player sandbox with about 200+ beautiful sectors populated by about 8 races, each with their own ships, technologies, stations, food supply chains, goods, etc.
2: You also can actually fly your ship (theres hundreds to choose from, some you'll have to capture but seriously you'll find something you love) itself with wasd or a joystick and dogfight unlike in EVE.
3: You can basically do whatever you want from escorting passengers or assassinating criminals to mining manually or by setting up individual stations, fill holes in the economy to help AI fractions or build self-sustaining war fleets or illegal drug empires and supply chains that exist only in a single sector or stretch across the universe via automated trade fleets operating out of closed-loop complexes.  You can of course be a pirate too, ejecting marines out of you cargo hold and watch them jet-pack onto a ship and cut their way through the hull and kill everything inside while you delicately keep the ships shields down on the outside (otherwise your poor meat-puppets will fry and you'll be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥cause training them is time sucking and expensive).  You can command huge fleets by piloting one ship, waiting till its on its last leg, ejecting into space, and teleporting into the cockpit of another one within 15km of you and keep hopping around as needed, some engagements can go on for a few hours if you want them too.  Heck you can even be a bloody day trader using the stock market.
The less good parts (and things to take note of to help you).
4: The interface takes some getting used to as its not all that intuitive but theres so many options and key bindings that I can see why making one would be hard.  You also need to remember that software upgrades and racial notoriety are the keys usually to success in the game.  You also need to pay attention to what areas need what goods and set up satellite networks to watch prices and supplies.
5:  The vanilla universe can be a bit dry though because the AI factions and even the pirates arent always aggressive enough towards you or each other.  The economy can also kind of sputter out in certain areas if you don't help it out.  That said, I highly recommend you go to the Egosoft forumsd an download either the X-Tended Mod or the XRM mod as that will solve this problem.  You wont be able to get achievements but who cares about that anyway?  It also might disable the plot but the plot missions are soo long and absurd for such little story in return that most players dont bother and just create thier own roleplay story as the play in the sandbox.
6:  I find managing large fleets to be difficult as there just arent enough options available for commanding large groups of them in meaningful ways.  The combination of SETA and autopilot can make things either crash into staions occasionally or make AI ships circle each other forever without ever being able to accurately hit each other.  Little bugs here and there like jumping through a gate in a large ship and accidentally ramming into a smaller ship on the other side and killing it, so the po-po comes after you.   Large trade fleets are tough to cause you rely so much on remote piloting by software commands and it becomes tough to keep track of them all and rememebring what routes you have going where, what sectors to avoid because of the Xenon and whatnot.  Again scripts and mods can fix a lot of this stuff though and I HIGHLY recommend modding the game as any issue you have with it or any added feature you would want someone has though of on Egosoft forums and has made a script for it.  The community is really helpful and dedicated, though it has shrunk some because of the unforgivable mess known as X;Rebirth  I should also mention theres a few exploits in the game too like nVidium mining and stock market abuse.
I hope you find this review to be of some use to you.  Be aware of what happened to me and tread carefully.  Its a great game for those with patience, intellect, and no hope of success in the real world.  It is probably a grave risk for anyone else.  If you do take the plunge on an X game though, this is the one to get.

Lost in the darkness of the hospital, Claire must find her way back to her mother with the help of her dog and the few trinkets she can find while avoiding the dangers creeping the halls.
PROS
+ Good atmosphere
+ Interesting idea/story
+ Cool characters/graphics
CONS
+ Too much walking around and backtracking (especially with few saves)
+ Confusing top down map with side scrolling gameplay
+ Blaring sound effects when enemy come on
+ Busy graphics make things confusing
From the intro I was into the game! It built a unique atmosphere that really pulled me in, but this soon passed for boredom and frustration.
The top-down map makes it confusing to make your way through the side-scrolling levels, especially when you're trying to run from a monster. Make one wrong turn and you are in a hallway with no exit. On top of that, the levels get very busy with all the pixel graphic gore, wreckage and whatnot making it more busy and confusing than it needs to be.
All the levels have dead ends, locked doors and fallen ceilings so you are doing A LOT of backtracking just to find a way through the level. Then you are supposed to spot and climb through these small vents in order to traverse level to level if you spot them. If you die because you didn't get away from a monster, you had better have found your way to one of the few save points in the game or you have to do it ALL AGAIN. This is why I quit.
It's not a terrible game at all, if you know what you are getting into. If there were more save points I would say definitely give it a try for a couple of buks. As it is, This game is way too frustrating and boring, especially for 10 dollars.

The gameplay in this odd stealth murder simulator is fascinating, and carried me all the way through until the end. The story is incredibly weak and the dialogue is cringe-worthy nearly all the time. Thankfully, this takes up only a tiny bit of the time you spend playing this game. And the game will suck you in, as each murder party is really a sort of puzzle - some of which take a few tries to figure out, while others are quite easy. The difficulty jumps up and down, rather than ramping up each level, but finishing a puzzle is generally rewarding and failure feels mostly fair.
It's a weird game. The story is awful beyond belief, predictable, and involves murdering hundreds of innocent party-goers. But it does have interesting mechanics and good puzzle design, that makes me want to recommend it. Unfortunately, the story giving the context that you are basically murdering innocent people makes the game less fun and the story, again, is so, so poorly written that I'm going to mention how bad it is again. So far, the combat in this game is awesome. You have little dynamic galaga-like spaceship and mech fighting levels that are fun as hell, and kind of reminiscient of the Gummi ship from Kingdom Hearts II only waaayy better. And then you have the third person sword-play combat (which is 99% of the games combat) which is so beautifully refined and awesome. For abilities you have these chips that take up a certain amount of space and a limited of allocated space to put them in, so you have to decide which power-ups will benefit your playstyle more and its very unique and original. The swordplay has weight and the combat becomes very instinctual and fluid once you get the hang of it. And if you're playing the game on 'hard' it is HARD AS ♥♥♥♥, which is awesome. Only about five hours in and the story is already building tension and mystery. Also, the soundtrack for this game is breathtaking. It reminds me of the original Ghost in the Shell film OST, which is what I think they were going for considering the many similarities between the two. So far, it's one of the best RPG's I've played since The Witcher 3, and the best game released within the past year, and I've only played so little of it. I had to come and leave a review because of this euphoric feeling I have from playing this game. It's truly a work of art.

This is a game that looks like the game I should like, but don't. The first major issue with this game is Linux performance. If you are a Linux user, I cannot recommend it, but ignoring that and trying to enjoy it, there are other things.
I like to forgive games for cliched stories and characters, but this game is a fantasy/medieval cliche parade that I just can't like. Lot's of people like the story, and good on them, but I think the writing is very lazy. The characters lack depth and the story is pretty much samey and boring. I just am not drawn to the story line at all. The lazily written dialogue is really just worsened by the fact that characters will repeat dialogue ad nauseum. I really don't identify with the protagonist either. Geralt is everything I am not, a gloomy mysterious hooded batman dude. I just don't connect with the character on any level, and the poor writing makes the character feel like an artificial attempt at being edgy. The humour in the game bombs pretty much every time as well, and I get that sinking feeling that you get when you are embarrassed for someone else's poor attempt at something like humour when I think about it.
The graphics in this game is really good. Things stand out fairly well and everything looks believable. Character animations are great and take a great step out of the uncanny valley. Weapons and battles look good and feel true to life. The game is poorly optimized. This isn't just true for Linux. I get some nasty framedrops on windows 10 too. If my machine can handle Max Payne 3 without framedrops TW2 should just work fine. Maybe my old AMD cpu is the problem. In any case framedrops ruin the gameplay. Console first maybe, then maybe PC users should avoid. Whatever the case, for me it was bad.
The audio in the game is very good. You know audio is very good when you hardly notice it. I seriously can't fault the audio in the game.
I tried with a mouse and keyboard and struggled with the controls. On a controller the controls were simpler but the camera was difficult to control.
Is the game bad? Certainly not. I think it's very good, but there are lots of games that are very good. It's the great games that stay with us and get us to stay invested in the story and the gameplay. I keep thinking I should love the game and when I play it again I find it to be average, but there is a good possibility that I will still play through it once and have fun with it.

Meridian: Squad 22 is a 4X RTS, in the style of the 90s games.
It is the second game in the Meridian series and is a massive improvement from the first one, Meridian: New World.
It's not required to have played New World to understand the story but it will give you more of an insight as to what's going on.
The game is made by one person and is focused on single player only.
In its current stage there’s 4 missions available but the story so far is progressing quite well and the missions have been fairly different from each other.
There are points throughout the story where you have choices to make which gives you different rewards.
You can only play as one faction but there are multiple AI factions with their own units for you to face.
There are three tech trees (combat, economy and defence) which lets you unlock new units, abilities and upgrades in an order you want.
This is done by collecting the three different research points (samples) scattered across the maps and making choices in the campaign.
In total there’s 17 different units available, including Infantry, mechs, tanks, naval and air.
There’s no Skirmish but there two alternative modes instead.
The first being World Conquest in which you fight on different territories against the AI and the difficulty increases from Easy to insane. As you get closer to the enemy’s HQ the harder the maps are. There are around 100 territories, give or take a few dozen, you can do as much or as few as you want to reach the main target. However the more maps you do the more samples you can collect.
Additionally there’s a fourth tech tree available in conquest that give you extra benefits.
Any excess points can be spent to ‘auto-win’ ‘Hard’ and ‘Very Hard’ territories to make it quicker and less of grind to get through.
The map generation is a little restricted in design.
The second one is Squad Missions, in which you can play single missions that provide a challange using a limited number of units.
For those that have played Meridian: New World here’s a few changes:
Graphics and animations have taken a large step forwards and also includes camera rotation and zoom.
More units are available and introduces naval units too but customising weapons isn’t possible anymore
AI and Path-finding has been improved and less hassle.
Commander’s abilities and research have been merged.
- Abilities have been altered to use cooldowns instead of using up energy. There are less abilities. Heal also repairs structures.
- Research are carried on through missions instead of building a new research lab each time.
Anyone that has played and liked it should probably like Squad 22 even more.
During closed beta, the developer listened to all feedback and many changes were made, lots of AI balancing and better performance.
He’s always active on the forums for all his games.
Worth a try for anyone that likes RTS games, particularly campiagn and a challanging AI.

This isn't a "quick review" or whatever. I had this game for about 4 or 5 days. I never played New World so going into the sequel I have no bias.
So right off the bat here is the TL;DR
+It's an RTS, I always welcome new RTS games
+Achievements
+Conquest mode. It's your basic capture the terrorities. You pick a terrority, invade to capture, get the resources for research that carry over.
+In my short time, no bugs experienced.
-Graphics are okay but in the desert everything is much brighter. It makes everything fuzzy. I guess they were going for that effect where you see a haze in the distance when its super hot outside.
-Singleplayer only. Don't get me wrong, I love singleplayer focused games. This is an RTS though, so many people will not buy this due to no multiplayer.
-One playable faction.
-From what I read the campaign is short. Like 4 missions short.
-AI gets incredible advantages in conquest mode. For example, you start out with 3 units, they get 5-8 with some already built buildings.
-The maps are tiny. It takes literally 5 seconds of exploring to find your opponent.
-No skirmish mode
-Naval units are awesome but all the bodies of water are tiny...like I'm talking smaller than a pond.
-Cannot zoom camera out too far. Camera always feels too close.
All in all, the game feels like a heavy grind. I "ugh"-ed everytime a new fight started because the battles act all just about the same. Even in Age of Empires where I do the same things in order as far as management goes, the AI on harder difficulties remain pretty unpredictible.
The game is in early access so maybe things will change for the better and I will update my review. Considering I can't put an hour in this game without immediately wishing I was playing something else...I am downvoting

This game♥♥♥♥♥♥♥with you- it has a few Hideo Kojima moments- such as one where looking at a specific item makes it appear that your computer has the blue screen of death- as well as a number of pretty well designed scares. The main enemies never stop being scary- mostly because they can kill you before you can say "where are those hellish screams coming from?"
This game actually, legitimately, terrifies me on occasion- but mostly it makes me grind my teeth in frustration and the fear is that I'll have to replay the same hour of gameplay again because I couldn't find a save point in time.
This game is limited by its eternal flowing forward and its dearth of save points- while gathering items to survive, I stumbled into the next chapter of the story (chapters which you cannot go back from), leaving me to miss out on several completion criteria- and hadn't saved in a while because there are only 2 or so save stations per level.
I can already hear the cries of "Git Gud" resounding- and if you play this game, you're gonna need to- enemies kill you fast, track you down mercilessly, loiter outside doors without warning, your direction walking changes depending on where you're positioned in the building- the list goes on.
Al in all, if there was an option for a "eh, play it if you have time and are bored" rating, I'd give it that. As it stands, there isn't. Wait for a steam sale to buy it.

If you want to get any X-game to try it out this is the one (do not play Rebirth first!), it has the least steep learning curve of the series and if you complete the main plot you have a couple million to start trading early rather than grinding back and forth between stations using SETA (you still do that, but not as much).
Combat
The big difference between this and X3:TC is the fact the Argon and Terrans are at war, so there are war sectors included which are interesting and can be dangerous to players, however apart from these sectors the universe feels more safe due to the absence of the Kha'ak. So apart from these sectors and a couple of pirate sectors the universe will feel completely harmless.
The combat is fun (at least in my opinion) as it requires many skills, during your game you will fly smaller fighters in one on one combat, engage against M7 frigates, and finally in Battleship M2 battles, each requiring different tactics to defeat. However the game has balancing issues in some respects, missile frigates can destroy anything, and are frequently spawned from combat missions. Put simply I saw 3 M2's, 2 M1's and pretty much everything else in a sector get destroyed by 1 missile frigate, as the cpu ships don't seem to understand missile defence, the only thing stopping it destroying my fleet was that it ran out of missiles.
Trade
Played an X-game before? Ok skip this part, there is very little change from previous X games in this section as the expansion   focuses mostly on combat, except for the inclusion of a stock exchange which allows you to invest in shares, and your actions in the universe affect the share prices based on demand and supply of the good you invested in. Issue being this makes the game very easy if you use exploits or have a complete monopoly within a sector.
For new people the trading is actually quite good at showing simple demand and supply economics (price elasticity may even be present!), put simply buy goods in high supply in low demand in one sector for a low price, next go to a sector where that good is in low supply and high demand. Sell it for profitsssssssss (meet the Teladi) and repeat over and over until you know exactly where the SETA key is.
Exploration
Other than about 2 sectors there is not many new regions to explore from X3:TC, but that does not take away the fact that it is a massive game, and will take you literally days for you to find all of the sectors due to a couple of hidden unknown sectors.
Summary
This game and the X series in general is not for everyone, as it requires the most amount of patience I have encountered in a video game (the many years of Football Manager and Championship Manager are not even close to this for time commitment) but if you stick with it you will uncover a jem of a game, and even if you do not want to spend the time just
install some mods (really recommended for new players as it adds so much to the game), change the players name to "Thereshallbewings" and script in your fleet of Excelsior and Galaxy class ships and the Normandy SR2 as your flagship frigate and take over the Galaxy!

Driven by a strong and compelling plot, satisfying gameplay, and an unforgetable soundtrack, few games can offer an experience comparable to NieR:Automata. What starts as a decently fun hack and slash game quickly evolves into a gripping rollercoaster of emotions.
It should be noted that this is the first game I've played in this series so my opinions will be reflective of that.
The Good:
- Absolutely amazing story
- Strong main cast
- Beautiful soundtrack
- Satisfying gameplay (combat, progression, gear)
- Open world
- Side quests that provide more meaning that just "do this, do that"
- Multiple endings
The Not so Good:
- 60 fps cap
- Infrequent crashing
- Limited/linear gear upgrades
- 900p, 30 fps cutscenes make transitions especially jarring
- Port is not very well optimized for its technical prowess
- Washed out colour palette (subjective)
- A few shockingly low resolution textures (i.e. the rusted red crate in the resistance camp)
- Hacking becomes repetitve after a while
Despite the existance of a few bugs [which will hopefully be addressed soon] and limitations that hold the game back, the unparalleled experience delivered by NieR:Automata easily outweighs its drawbacks. This is one of the few purchases as of recent that I've felt was worth the full price tag.

Claire was a great buy for me. As a fan of Silent Hill I've been scrounging the depths of the horror genre, and part of my search led me to this game. At the time it was on sale (for only a couple of dollars), and I love to support indie developers and try new things, so I decided to buy it. Definitely worth the buy! Not only was this game similar in horror aspects to Silent Hill, but even the sounds of the game, map layouts, and story were very similar and did very well for the overall feel of the game.
Do not get this game if you do not enjoy puzzles, Silent Hill gameplay (extensive map checking, awkward camera angles, learning to run, etc), or sanity levels (this is a huge part of the later reaches of the game). However, if you appreciate good stories that tie into the horror aspects, a strong female protagonist, interesting NPCs, dogs (Anubis is just plain adorable!), and exploring the deep recesses of the mind then this is the game for you!
I would reach to give this game a 9/10 because it fulfilled my horror buzz, the story was amazing, Claire and Anubis were wonderful, and the graphics (though not the best in the world) were quite appealing to me. The only point I would take away would be for the gameplay itself. It got quite hard at times because you can't fight the enemies and they constantly chase you through doors all the while your sanity meter drops you down to horrified in a second in certain areas and you lose the rest of your health because you are scared. It's very hard to get away, and Claire's stamina is not very good, so you get very slow very fast. The only other problem I had with it was the bug which, whenever you hit the accept button on the menu screen made you hit the accept button on the actual map as well. I would be hiding in a closet from an enemy, pull out my map on my menu, hit accept, and I would die because it would bring me out of the closet as well. Regardless of the criticisims this game is wonderful, and is definitely worth the buy for classic horror fans!

Three words can describe how my experience was in this game. Purely. Justifiably. Amazing. When you first enter X3 you are swamped by a non-tutorial, up-close, unforgiving, and dangerous universe. It takes a little practice to learn the ropes of the game; exploration, trading, and battle. This can be a very dangerous world or a very  safe one, depending on who you chose to be. It is best not to think of a single directive but more long term and while being a cutthroat pirate maybe fun and exciting it does not however pay very well, unless you hit a large target. This however is extremely difficult and takes a lot of preparation. So, whether or not you are planning your large heist you have to encounter trading at some point. This concept can take a little getting used to but my recommendation would be to go around trading energy cells until you have a good amount of cash, all the while looking at rising and falling stocks at the exchange.. Then invest in some stocks. (Yes the game has its own living and breathing stock exchange that can be very hard and frustrating but can create a very large payout to those who figure it out.) After you gain a sum of money and are sitting happily in your battlecrusier struggling to maneuver the shipping lanes, look for the best place to get weapons, build some stations, and go exploring. Be cautious though, there is always someone who wants you dead. It is very dangerous and yes, you may be large and have enough cannons to block out the sun, but a well aimed missile can kill you and end your game. All in all 9/10.

If youre gonna have a party, then you better be ready to party hard with all the traditional favors; drinks, dancing, music, knives, poison, bombs, and bears. Ok, maybe you
shouldn't party that hard personally but that's how you do it in Party Hard by Indie Dev Pinoki Games. Party Hard is a game about a man who is fed up with his neighbors
constant partying and he justs wants to get some sleep. However that man is also a brutal psychopath choosing to end the party by any means neccesary without stopping
until going around the country and crashing each party he encounters. You'll enter each party armed with nothing but a knife where the only goal is to kill everyone.
You also have the capability to rig traps, sabatoge environments, pick up other weapons and tools, and also call in support from time to time. Regardless of your approach
you have to be careful and not be seen doing any of these attacks. The overall system works very well with party goers only calling you out if they see you commit the crime,
or walk in on you standing near dead bodies.
The environmental attacks work as a sort of freebie and won't alert people to your pressence but if they see the dead body
they're likely to call the cops which tends to make things more difficult until they leave. If I had one complaint here, it's that I wish there was even more environmental
interaction. With the procedral style level design these objects change position making it interesting with room for replayability, but I still would like to see more to
interact with. What tends to happen is you stab a few victims, hide a few bodies and start activating traps, only to run out and wait for the npc's to break away from the
crowd one by one thus repeating this step over and over. It's still satisfying to single out victims, but the game gets really exciting when you unleash a big attack forcing
the scragglers into other surrounding traps.
That brings me to the overall design and tone. Party Hard is a modern day 16-bit game in a half cocked birds eye view, which definitely brings a comparison to the similar
styled game Hotline Miami. But, where hotline miami was a fast paced shoot & slug fest, Party Hard takes things a bit slower invoking a lot of technical planning and
thinking. I think this is great because rather than be a copy, it's a very different game that will appeal to the same audience. If you enjoyed Hotline Miami, and enjoy
puzzle like stealth then you'll enjoy this. The music will also likely get you pumped and excited as you play. Right away I was bobbing my head and enjoying the music the
moment I started until it was over.
The story was good as well with a recollective style narrative involving a cop and interviewer discussing the path the murderer took. It kept me hooked in and was very well
done with a few twists and decent voice acting. It took me a bit over 7 hours to complete but I'll definitely be playing again to try and get faster times and better
scores.
Overall Party Hard is a game you should play. It has good replayability, the gameplay is smooth and I encountered only a few technical issues. Its gritty story and
violent nature are entertaining and the soundtrack is just awesome. The only negatives are as I mentioned, the enironments could use a bit more interaction, and I would like
to have had more weapon options and traps. With that I'm giving Party Hard an A-. This is definitely one to pick up and I wouldn't be surprised if there is a second one.

I really, really want to give the game a good rating. Because it just has the potential to get there. It is unique, has an amazing atmosphere and rewarding gameplay. At the moment, however, all those merits are overshadowed by a few critical game design flaws that make you want to quit after dying for the Xth time. I will summarize here the main ones:
(Note: I played the game co-op with a friend)
1. Pressing ESC does not pause. You think the game is paused but it actually runs in the background. And of course you die within seconds of not paying attention (wolf, heat, food, whatever). Next thing you do is try to find the hidden "pause" button and stumble upon the "sleep" function in the Shelter. You think "that's it" and run to the door to grab the pizza that just arrived. Tough luck mate -in the meantime woke up and died of hunger. Why can't you just add a friggin' PAUSE option there?? Dying is really painful in this game, it shouldn't happen because you get up to pee. Which brings me to the next point:
2. Dying is unnecessarily punishing. To sum it up: when you die you a) lose all your ability points (gained through tiresome, repetitive grinding) b) need to rebuild and upgrade your buildings (again more unnecessary grinding) and - worst of all - c) you need to run all the way from the starting area to where you were before without a single protective item or ability (except one piece of candy which does not do much). Did the devs actually test their own game? How are you supposed to wade through hordes of wolves to the other side of the map where your items dropped where you died? The only way to do so is to rebuild on the way while your teammates - no joke - simply wait for you to do so. Which can take 10-15 minutes depending on where you died last! Did the devs forget that this is a co-op game? Where is the fun if you force people to wait doing nothing? (the whole point is that you progress the story together!).
3) Related to last point: no markers on the map for players and death areas. If you move a bit faster than your teammates you simply lose them. If you decide to pick up that berry or mushroom, you lose them. If you decide to hunt a deer alone, you lose them. Wtf is that? Why can't you just add a colored marker so that we can find each other? And don't even get me started on finding the place where your items dropped on death...
4) There are pitfalls on the map, which are easy to oversee. If you fall into one of those gaping holes, you die immediately, and there is no way to go in there again. Which means say goodbye to all your items forever. Really devs? Is that your definition of game progress? I quit the game immediately when this happened.
Summing up: I am more than willing to change my rating as soon as the above is addressed. But I have rage quit the Wild Eight already too many times due to the above and still cannot fathom how you can screw up such a nice game with so obvious errors.

Back when this game first came out, I obtained a *cough* demo version, to test it out and see if I wanted to actually buy it.
My initial thoughts were that the game really just wasnt as good as the other borderlands. On top of that, I really didnt like Handsome Jack from Borderlands 2.
Then the borderlands pack hit the Humble bundle store.
I bought it and played the first one again and it was a nostalgic trip of bliss. I enjoyed it so much that I just went ahead and bought all of the games (Pre-sequel was higher up on the bundle)
Boy were my first impressions wrong. I freaking love this game. Handsome Jack is an amazing character in this game, and seeing him turn into the Handsome Jack from BL2 is an incredible story.
The Guns are even more unique than before, Cold elemental damage is probably one of my favorite things. But I've always taken the elemental class trees. In BL1, all the gun companies just altered their stats a little. In this game, every gun compnay varries greatly between each other. A Jakobs Sniper rifle vs a Vladov Sniper are two completely different things. One is basically a fully automatic Lead raining fury ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LMG and the other is a 50 cal. head exploiding sniper.
While at first I thought all the characters were boring and I didnt really want to play as any of them, I bought the Baroness and she is INCREDIBLY fun to play. Her dialogue is less so fun.
After beating the game I tried out Claptrap, absolutley hilarious dialogue, his action skill has tons of different effects that varry depending on the situation you're in. I dont think I've seen all of his possible action skill effects yet. For instance, if everyone is dying and you use his action skill, he gets a medic gun, or if you kill someone with a melee attack and use it, he beceoms a psycho with a giant saw axe thing. You know the ones. I feel like on the surface the characters seem shallow and boring but if you actually play them all, they'll end out being more fun than you'd think.
One thing I didnt like was that some of the NPC's that I loved so much werent in the game. Dr.Zed is one of my favorites. But since you're not on pandora, it makes sense that they wouldnt be there. Still though, their replacements are enjoyable. I still wish I could hear zed say "Who needs a real doctor when you have my machines and their... Scary needles"

is a short point and click adventure where puzzles are -for the most part- logical and straightforward.
It took me almost 4 hours to finish my first play-through, and a big part of that was trying to figure out the only puzzle I found to be illogical. If you are faced with the same difficulty, maybe Achievements name can give you a clue.
A second complete play-through, where I aimed for the remaining achievements, took just 35 minutes.
The game premise may give a hint of a dark, weird world. And that's exactly what you get. Nika, a 7 year-old, is faced with themes as alcohol, violence and sex... weird sex, you don't want to know about it. I found it as borderline inappropriate as funny. There is some clever writing in here, specially the dialogue with certain couple that seem to know too much about the world Nika lives in.
At first, I was not enjoying the graphic style and the cumbersomeness of actions and controls. Changing resolution in-game had some unpredictable behavior for me (I could never get back to Full HD) so I resorted to the configuration file. Disabling that big mouse cursor and changing the font made a great impact, and I finally settled on the weirdness of the graphics. After all, they match with the bizarre story and cast of characters.
I would have liked to see more work in the sound aspect. There is no background sound and sound effects are really limited. Music is cheerful and cute, I'll give them that. There are, however, multiple dialogue options, which I appreciate.
It also includes cards and achievements which are not really hard to get. Cards took a while to drop, tough.
In terms of structure, this review has been a failure. But I would like to conclude saying that, considering its price tag, I recommend this game!

I'll start by saying this, mini-golf games are not my cup of tea.  I'm not a big fan of them and while I've played a few they are a genera I tend to ignore.  That being said, there are many positive qualities about Fantasy Fairways.  The sound design for the game is lovely and relaxing.  The art is pretty and the animations are interesting and just as beautiful at times.  I enjoy the little touches in the game, like how the flowers get sucked into the hole after the ball goes in.  The game offers a nice challenge as well.  It isn't just try to get the ball in the hole and avoid the opsticles.  It challenges the player to think and to really figure things out.  Getting a hole in one is going to take a fair bit of skill and spatial reasoning.  It is this unique spin to the game that really makes it stand out from the rest in its genera.  (Honestly, I think they should add puzzling to the genera list.)
All of this being said, the game is not perfect.   It is still in its infancy and it shows through the various glitches and limited features.  The tutorial especially could use some work as the player has to figure out a lot of the features for themselves.  However, the foundation for a good, if not a great, game is there.  This is a excellent game for those who enjoy challenging puzzles and people who like mini-golf games.  I look forward to seeing how it evolves.

There's a lot to say about this game. There's so much about it that I loved, and though it has its flaws, I think the pros far outweigh the cons.
First and foremost, the real pleasure of this game is in exploring the world. Its environment and ambiance are fantastic. The art style, the many yet small world-building details, the sense of history and mythology, and the characters populating Mousewood all give layers upon layers to this world. And that's just the area in and around Mousewood--as the plot progresses, more worlds are opened to the main character, Jerry, and though they're less detailed than the "home world" of Mousewood, they're each interesting and beautiful in their own ways. They all contribute to the overall environment. I was definitely immersed.
Secondly, the story. (I won't give an overview of the basic plot, because the previews and official overview tell you everything you need to know on that front.) In the early stages of the game, I wasn't sure if the central plot would really solidify, and that might be one of the game's flaws--the main plot takes some time to launch. In the beginning of the game Jerry spends most of his time helping the inhabitants of Mousewood in small ways. The purpose is obviously to familiarize the player with Mousewood and with all the characters, and in that sense it did contribute to the world-building; however, it did feel a bit slow in places. When hints of the central plot did show through, they seemed a bit disjointed, all vaguely connected but with no discernible purpose or relationship. It was almost like soup that wouldn't thicken, and it did distract me at times. However, as I got farther into the game (especially at about the halfway point), the hints started coming together. The soup thickened. And the further I played, the more I found the story to be multilayered and imaginative. The final scenes of the game really click everything into place. The end made me want to immediately replay the game so I could more fully appreciate all the hints dropped in the beginning.
I'm not sure if this is a pro or con, but the puzzles were largely unremarkable. There were a few stand out puzzles I enjoyed, but for the most part they were pretty obvious.
The real flaws of the game, in my opinion, are more mechanical than substantive. The voice acting is often overwhelmed by the music/ambient noises in the game (bird calls, wind, bug noises, etc.). I'm not really sure what the problem is, if it's particular to my computer or to the game's software (I think it's probably the latter), but in many scenes I could just barely hear the voices with my speaker volume turned almost all the way up--which is a shame, because I liked the voice acting that I could actually hear. Sometimes there are strangely-placed, longish pauses in dialogue that feel awkward and make scenes drag. And though I do love the art, the moving animation can be a bit stilted.
Whether or not you buy the game depends on the experience you're looking for. If you want something fast-paced and high-action, I would pass. If you're looking for a fun, detailed world with colorful characters, and you have the patience to wait until the very end of the game to understand the full complexity of the plot, then I would highly recommend The Night of the Rabbit.

Currently the peak game of the X Universe, Albion Prelude is the final game to be created on Egosoft's old game engine. Ships, systems and stations are at an all time high in both quantity and diversity.
For those not knowledgeable about the X series, it is a space sim that offers the ability toooooooo.... explore, fight, trade, complete plots, do random missions, build stations, build empires, construct fleets, secure sectors and fly any ship class from frighter to fighter to battleship. The downside really is the system layout - you have hundreds of systems... which are all squares filled with randomly plomped stations. Most systems have no real allure or use, so the atmosphere can be a little meh. But the gameplay is great.
If you want a space sim sandbox with a multitude of possibilities, X3AP should be your choice, even over X Rebirth at this stage. And if you're interested in X Rebirth but want to wait until it is improved, this game is your friend. If you want the whole backstory to this game, get the entire X series and play through each games' plot one by one.

The funny part about the items, is that they don`t tell you, what the item can do. You either have to look at your stats, or try to shot, in order to see what the item did for you. If nothing changes, it can get really diffecult to find out what the item did, and you have to remember what meny items did, so you don`t end up downgrading youself.

There is an arcade, where you can gamble, with your money and win prices.

This 2-D pixaleated horror game is about a girl named Claire who after visiting her mother one day in the hospital suddenly finds the hospital abandoned and for the most part in rubbles. She must explore the hospital in order to find out what happend.
While there aren't what I would call jump scares, the hospital environment is ominous. Claire will encounter dark 'ghosts' (not sure if that's what they are) which she can only outrun. Later when she gains her companion dog he can alert her to oncoming ghosts. There are a few puzzles to complete, and a storyline begins to emerge the further you get in this "maze". Overall, its a really nice game, good amount of creepy, and has a good storyline. There are multiple endings depending on how you play, so play keeping that in mind!
There are a couple cons that were a bit infuriating; the amount of doors you have to walk through and their confusing positions. Some of them are so close its hard to figure out where at times I am going on the map. The map is mostly useful, with a couple of time it can also be confusing like the crawlspaces and mysterious floors you land on with no maps. Also, Claire has the stamina of a moridbly obese geriatric.  She'll literally run for a second and be out of breathe. Believe me, even if I was in horrendous shape, if I saw a creepy spirit following me I would find stamina from somewhere. I'm not a huge fan of stamina in games (because I like my character to run on default), but if it has to be put in to boost up the difficulty I wish it was at least more realistic.
Tl; dr Awesome simple horror game, few cons but nothing that would ruin it for me personally. Worth it!

This is arguably the best call of duty to date. It depends wether or not you are a Treyarch fan or Infinity Ward fan. Most fans of Call Of Duty say Modern Warfare is the best one, but I always was more keen on Treyarchs version of COD. Dont get me wrong, I know that COD MW innovated alot and changed the multiplayer to the better and that their campaign were a thrill. I also know that COD MW also changed the genre, but when it comes to the best of the best I would say that this game is the best... of the best.
The campaign is special and unique. I havent seen anyone else do the COD campaign like that. It got me interested from begining to end as it isnt just a war story about a soldier (as most call of duty games) but it also involves conspiracy theories, phsyciatric challenges and monkeys. Okey, the last one is not as important, but I am serious about the other things and really believe that this is the best campaign. Maybe that has to do with the setting. I fell in love with the cold war (not as in I liked the cold war, but more as in I like the story behind it). The only COD game that isnt modern/futuristic or about the second world war. I kinda hope it stays that way, because they did a good job and I dont really think they could make it better. I have heard rumors about Sledgehammer making a game set during the cold war and I hope its false. Would be nice to make a game that is set in the past, but make it about something else. Give us something new (and as most cod players mean with something new, give us more content dont change up the mechanics). To get back on track, the campaign is something that you have to try out for your self.
The multiplayer was also pretty great. It stayed fast paced with memorable maps, nice weapon balancing and fun game modes. The perks werent too bad either, although I will admit that "second chance" perk was a bad one. Luckily most servers on PC has banned that perk. Killstreaks return and all of them serve a purpose. There is more focus on party modes and that is always fun. I really enjoy what they did with cod points. No, Im not talking about the latest version of cod points where you actually have to spend money on it. Im talking about the in-game currency that you use to unlock camoes, weapons, attatchements and of course face paint. You could play wager matches and gamble your money to maybe win more money. Those matches were intense, but no other COD game has tried to replicate it. It is a Black Ops only experience.
While the multiplayer and campaign were exeptional in COD MW, the game still lacked a memorable and fun coop mode. Well, COD BO steps up their game with continuing on COD Zombies. The problem with COD BO2 and COD BO3 is that the maps are made for zombie fans. You might think that im weird for complaining about them making maps for the zombie fans, but what I mean is that the maps in those games were not casual friendly. I enjoyed the maps in those games, even my favourite zombie maps comes from those games, but I am a COD Zombies fan. I have an interest in it and I am patient enough to learn the maps. However, anyone who isnt like me will have a problem figuring out what is going on and what to do. The last maps are all about objectives. The steps you have to take just to pack-a-punch in those games are completely bonkers (yes I used the word bonkers to describe it). Playing public on those maps are so hard. You just have to hope that you meet a player that is also a zombie fan. For a casual game like COD, the maps in BO2 and BO3 were so so amazingly not casual that people just stuck to multiplayer and then got bored. I understand why they would complain too. COD is a 3 for 1 deal. You get multiplayer, campaign and coop. When you only get multiplayer and campaign, you can feel a little bit scammed. Like it wasnt worth the money. In this game they manage to keep the maps casual while also adding easter eggs, story and tricks for the Zombie fans. So a zombie expert could have just as much fun as a casual player.
All in all, the game is good and I completely recommend it. If you like Call Of Duty, then you wont be dissapointed. Buy this game. The only complaint about the pricing is the DLCs. They can be expenisve, so just buy them on sale. There are no seasonpass on PC so make sure that you wait for the right time to buy them all. The DLCs is mainly for people who are interested in zombies. You dont need it either. You still got 3 fun zombie maps without it. At last, I do know it says that I have 3 hours on this game, but I played it a lot on console before switching to PC. I bought it again on steam because I just had to have this masterpiece in my steam library. Either way, I doubt that you will actually read all of this so Im basically talking to myself at this point. Just buy it and try it. You wont regret if you are a fan of the series.
Edit: I have now many more hours into this game since I decided to revisit the game. I can tell you that I still stand by everything I have said in this review and it makes me recommend it even more.

This is honestly one of the most memorable games i've played in a long time. The characters create an emontional story while the combat kept me entertained and challenged throughout my 20 hours digging straight through the main story. The best part is i'm still not done and still have more to work towards.
I'm afraid that many people will stop playing when they see the credits roll for the first time. Its something I almost did, but i'm thankful I loaded my save again. This game features multiple endings, so keep playing to the very end.
The music is astounding, even though i'm not the biggest fan of the vocals. I'm hoping steam will include a OST download at some point...
On regards to the PC port, I had no issues with gameplay on my 1080 card. I hope others will get their fixes too. The only issue i had graphically was with the light rays on environments and characters, particularly in the side scroller sections. The glare makes a ugly blur and looks blocky around the character heads.
The RPG elements are a nice addition, including weapons and chips that augment stats or give extra combat/ support functions. I can't really say this is a choice-driven game aside from persuing the endings, but its not an issue. Once you've FINISHED the game to the very end, you'll be allowed to backtrack through the story, whilst keeping all progress, levels, chips, and upgrades.
Overall its been an outstanding experience and hope to see more games like this.
Some cons:
-Invisible walls around some buildings, mainly the city.
-Not entirely voiced. The main story progression is fully voiced, but most sub-quests and convesations are text.
-Permanent loss of chip upgrades if you die again before reaching your body, like how Dark Souls has you loose souls. Upgraded chips can be purchased towards endgame, but there are rare chips with reduced memory usage that would be a pain to loose.
-Keyboard/mouse gameplay was difficult for me, particulaly in trying to aim the Pod's fire. Controllers are recommended.

Got this as a gift but I would have easily paid money for this game. People are right when they say it has the Silent Hill vibes, and there's even references to the series, but it's more than that. I'd classify the gameplay style as more... amnesia-esque. You don't fight the monsters, just run and hide. It still has it's own idenity, but these aspects are found in other horror games. But, as long as it's not a shameless copy and paste or clone, I like it when people learn what gameplay ideas work from other successful games. They took good ideas and evolved them not into something that's neccessarily better (that's all up to opinion) but something that is different.
The art style is extremely refreshing, too. Rather unique in my opinion. The enemies/monsters remind me a bit of Yume Nikki, but they are still very much their own style. And the scenery is AMAZING. It works so well. The sound design, when added with it, give it a really good atmosphere that sucks you in. It's quite an immersive world.
If I were to criticise one thing, it would be that it doesn't understand quite what made Silent Hill 2 (and 3, but 2 is my personal favorite) the perfect horror game. It isn't... subtle. Granted, once you get into SH2, it goes on strong, but during the beginning the atmosphere, while eerie, isn't in your face with weirdness. I feel like Claire kinda starts off a bit too... jarring. Rather than making things immediately horrifying, start off by making things just weird and scary. Add subtle things. Ease us into the nightmare. It creates better immersion, and makes it feel more "real".
In the end though, great game. I love it. If you like survival horror that isn't all zombies, then this is definitely something to look at.

Couple of hours in. Here's what I reckon so far (bearing in mind there's not much to it, two hours feels like enough to judge).
1. It's kind of fun, in general. The standard business of picking folks off alone or in groups is enjoyable for a while. Not super enjoyable for very long, but it'll do for a bit.
2. Elements of the map design are random and this isn't really a good thing. Have done maps that felt really sparse in terms of traps, or that had no food to poison and these can be a chore because you're basically just stabbing everybody. Also the problem with this randomness in a game where you're trying to set high scores is that your high score is going to depend on a good map spawn, which renders the scoring system moot.
3. It's a bit too simple and a bit too random. Way back when I used to play a game called Skool Daze on the Spectrum about being a prankster in a school, and it feels about that kind of level of sophistication. And that was about twenty five years ago. Feels like more could have been done in terms of interacting with the crowd or reading their behaviour. Not asking for realism, just more elements to play with.
4. The traps are often a bit rubbish. You can have loads of fun with poison, especially when people start to blame each other for it, but the others vary between being amazing bordering on overpowered and just being a slightly more cumbersome alternative to a stab. Doing things like blowing up a methlab ought to have more to it.
5. Graphics aren't great. And yes I know Pixel Art is a style, it's not about that. The style is fine, it's just not implemented very well. There is no visual indicator for how far people can see, you have to guess a lot of the time which walls, such as they are, can be seen through, or what height things are at, if they are even at a different height. The indicators for when you've got the cops after you and for when somebody has seen something and blamed another person for it, they work well, but there could be more.
All things considered, it's not offensively bad, it's not hellish, it's not like I've come out of playing it going THIS SUCKS, but it's not Hotline Miami, it's not Postal, it's not even Skool Daze. Some people are going to embrace this game and love it and squeeze it and call it George. If you think you might be one of those people, take a punt on it. Might get lucky and love it. For everybody else, probably not worth the time, and probably only worth the money in a sale.
